The wireless communication device: acquires, from a predetermined wireless slave device included in one or more wireless slave devices different from the wireless communication device, unrelated transmission information that is transmission information wirelessly transmitted to a master device, corresponding to the predetermined wireless slave device, in accordance with the predetermined time division multiple access scheme and that includes identification information identifying the predetermined wireless slave device, the unrelated transmission information being acquired at the time of the wireless transmission; on the basis of the identification information included in the unrelated transmission information, the acquisition time of the unrelated transmission information, and information relating to a transmission sequence, determines a predetermined time slot for the wireless communication device to transmit the predetermined information to the master device corresponding thereto in accordance with the predetermined time division multiple access scheme; and transmits the predetermined information. Consequently, provided is wireless communication technology that enables information collection using high-speed and highly reliable wireless communication.

outputs.L1: A wireless communication device is configured to wirelessly transmit predetermined information stored therein to a corresponding master device at predetermined transmission intervals in accordance with a predetermined time-division multiple-access scheme. The wireless communication device acquires, at the time of wireless transmission, unrelated transmission information from a predetermined wireless slave device among one or more wireless slave devices different from the wireless communication device. The unrelated transmission information is wirelessly transmitted, in accordance with the predetermined time-division multiple-access scheme, to a master device corresponding to the predetermined wireless slave device and includes identification information identifying the predetermined wireless slave device. Based on the identification information included in the unrelated transmission information, the time at which the unrelated transmission information is acquired, and information relating to a transmission sequence, the wireless communication device determines a predetermined time slot in which to transmit the predetermined information to its corresponding master device in accordance with the predetermined time-division multiple-access scheme, and transmits the predetermined information in the determined time slot. Accordingly, wireless communication technology is provided that enables information collection through high-speed, highly reliable wireless communication.
outputs.L2: A wireless communication device is arranged to send, at specified intervals, predefined information stored by the device to its associated master device using a prescribed time-division multiple-access scheme. During wireless transmission, the device obtains unrelated transmission information from a selected wireless slave device among one or more slave devices other than itself. This unrelated transmission information is transmitted wirelessly, under the same prescribed time-division multiple-access scheme, to the master device associated with the selected slave device and contains identification data that identifies that slave device. Using the identification data, the time at which the unrelated transmission information was obtained, and transmission-sequence-related information, the wireless communication device selects a designated time slot in which to transmit its predefined information to its corresponding master device in accordance with the prescribed time-division multiple-access scheme. The device then sends the predefined information in the selected slot. This technology allows information to be collected through wireless communication with both high speed and high reliability.
outputs.L3:
The wireless communication device periodically transmits predetermined information to its corresponding master device using a time division multiple access (TDMA) scheme. During wireless transmission, the device also acquires unrelated transmission information sent by another wireless slave device to that device’s corresponding master device. The acquired information includes identification data associated with the other wireless slave device and the time at which the information was acquired.

Based on the identification data, the acquisition time, and information indicating the applicable transmission sequence, the wireless communication device selects an appropriate time slot for transmitting its own information. By coordinating transmission timing in this manner, the system reduces communication conflicts and uses available time slots efficiently, thereby enabling high-speed and highly reliable collection of information over the wireless network.
outputs.L4:
A wireless communication device operating in a TDMA environment collects information from transmissions sent by slave devices belonging to other communication groups. For each overheard transmission, the device identifies the transmitting slave device and records associated information, such as the time at which the transmission was acquired and data indicating the transmission sequence or slot pattern used by that device. The wireless communication device analyzes this information to determine which TDMA slots are occupied or are likely to be occupied by nearby devices.

Based on the analysis, the device selects a time slot that is expected to have a low probability of interference or collision. It then uses the selected slot to transmit information to its own master device. The slot-selection process may be repeated or updated as additional transmissions are detected, allowing the device to adapt to changes in surrounding wireless traffic.

By using actual transmissions from unrelated slave devices as a basis for selecting a transmission opportunity, the device can reduce contention, retransmissions, and communication delays without requiring direct coordination between separate communication groups. This enables information from multiple wireless devices to be collected at high speed and with high reliability, even in an environment in which several TDMA networks operate simultaneously.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a wireless communication device that selects a TDMA transmission slot by overhearing another slave device’s transmission, using its identification information, acquisition time, and transmission-sequence information.
counterfactuals.output: A wireless communication device and method are provided for selecting a transmission slot in a time-division multiple-access (TDMA) communication system. The device receives, by overhearing a transmission from another slave device, identification information associated with the other slave device, acquisition-time information indicating a time at which the transmission was acquired, and transmission-sequence information indicating a position or order of the transmission within a TDMA sequence. The device determines timing information for the TDMA system based on the acquisition-time information and the transmission-sequence information, and selects an available transmission slot based at least in part on the determined timing information and the identification information. The device thereafter transmits in the selected transmission slot, thereby enabling slot selection without first receiving dedicated slot-assignment information from a master device.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical abstract for a wireless communication technology in which multiple slave-master pairs share a predetermined time-division multiple-access scheme without centralized slot coordination, while maintaining fast and reliable data collection.
counterfactuals.output: A wireless communication technology is presented for rapid, reliable data collection from multiple independently operating slave–master pairs sharing a predetermined time-division multiple-access (TDMA) frame. Each pair autonomously determines its transmit and receive slots using synchronized frame timing and a deterministic slot-selection function derived from pair-specific identifiers, without centralized slot assignment or inter-pair signaling. Potential collisions are mitigated through distributed slot hopping, acknowledgment-based collision detection, and adaptive reselection within the fixed TDMA structure. Slave devices transmit buffered measurements during designated short-duration uplink slots, while corresponding masters provide acknowledgments and timing corrections in associated downlink slots. Guard intervals, channel diversity, retransmission scheduling, and bounded-latency recovery improve robustness to clock drift, interference, and transient packet loss. The resulting architecture supports concurrent deployment of numerous uncoordinated pairs while preserving low latency, high collection reliability, deterministic power consumption, and scalable spectrum reuse.
